summary.text: Bill Keating is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 9th District. A lawyer, he served in both chambers of the Massachusetts legislature and as Norfolk County district attorney before winning election to Congress in 2010. He serves on the House Armed Services and Foreign Affairs committees.

paragraphs.text: Born September 6, 1952, in Norwood, Massachusetts, and raised in Sharon.

Earned a bachelor's degree (1974) and master's degree (1982) from Boston College and a law degree from Suffolk University (1985). Wikipedia describes the master's as an MBA and says he later became a partner at the law firm Keating & Fishman.

Elected to the Massachusetts House of Representatives in 1976, at age 24, and served there until 1984, when he won a Norfolk and Suffolk seat in the Massachusetts State Senate; he served in the State Senate into the late 1990s.

Elected Norfolk County District Attorney in 1998, defeating the incumbent, and was reelected without opposition in 2002 and 2006. His office launched a Norfolk Anti-Crime Council and a drug court pilot program, and laid the groundwork for a Children's Advocacy Center in the county.

Won the open 10th District seat in the 2010 election, defeating Republican state Rep. Jeff Perry, and took office in January 2011. After redistricting in 2012, he ran in the redrawn 9th District, which he has represented since 2013.

Serves on the House Armed Services Committee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee, where he is the top Democrat on the Subcommittee on Europe. His work has focused on district issues such as the fishing industry and nuclear safety, according to Wikipedia.
A co-sponsor of Medicare for All in 2019, he is seeking an eighth term in 2026; he won the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary over Craig Swallow.
Lives in Bourne with his wife, Tevis; they have two adult children, according to Wikipedia.
